title: The Slow Library
summary: Shrine-Keeper Toll is migrating the mid-span lending shelf to Saltmouth for storm season — eleven crates of annotated books on a donkey-cart retrofitted with hover-skids, which the donkey has noticed. Escort the Slow Library down the glassroad; the crosswinds on the Slick Mile have strong literary opinions.

objectives.label: Meet Toll and the donkey at the mid-span shrine
Escort the Slow Library — keep the wagon warm, stay close
See the first crate onto the job-board shelf

offer.text: Rider. Season's turning and my lending shelf cannot winter on the span — books hate damp worse than borrowers. Eleven crates, one donkey-cart, hover-skids from Ketch's 'experimental' bin, and a route home through the Slick Mile's crosswinds. I require a shepherd with an engine.

The donkey has audited the skids and files them as sorcery. The cart moves at reading pace. You will be tempted, courier, to scout ahead and be efficient. Resist. A library unescorted is just tinder with plot.
Eleven crates of books, one sceptical donkey, four kilometres of glass canyon. What's the worst the wind does?
Two seasons ago the wind took a whole crate of sermons over the south rim unpunished. The crater floor there now converts passing lizards. I do not joke about the Sermon Drift, rider. Stay close.

accept.text: We roll when the lamps do. Order of march: the donkey sets the pace, the skids complain in B-flat, and you, rider, are the margin of the page — you keep the print from blowing off the edge. On the Mile, ride the windward flank and break the gusts before they reach the crates.

Ketch here — Toll took my skid rig, the maniac. It hums off-key 'cause I tuned it to a kettle. Kid, hover near the wagon, not ahead of it; convoy rules. If the crosswind stands the hair up off the donkey, lean over the crates till it passes. Books are cargo. Donkeys are crew. Priorities.
Riding as a bookmark. New personal speed record: slowest.
'The fastest road is the one the slowest friend survives.' Mine. Feel free to write it on the cart. The donkey has expressed no opinion, which for a donkey is rave review.

complete.text: Eleven crates delivered, zero sermons embarked to the lizards, one donkey promoted to Hang-Donkey Emeritus by general acclamation. The shelf lives at the job board through season's end. Borrow freely, rider. Return before the storm does.

For your fee and your shepherding: my copy of the visitor's book of the mid-span chapel — two centuries of who stopped, who signed, who lied about signing. You'll find Rill's mark in it. Page-hand for page-hand, courier, we keep each other's route.
The donkey's looking at me like I owe him a review.
Then write him one. Short words. He annotates.
